groups.title: Frequentative foundation and shape choice
groups.proposal: Treat the frequentative as a productive derivation on any open typed verbstem. Because Andrews gives no strict rule that predicts which reduplicative shape cooperates with a particular stem, let the user choose short-vowel-plus-glottal-stop, long-vowel, or short-vowel formation; derive the copied consonant and vowel from Source shape.
groups.writingJob: Apply the selected frequentative shape to an open typed Source, copy the licensed initial consonant and vowel material, preserve the three-way shape inventory, and carry the frequentative Result into the normal finite grammar without using Canvas examples as a stem list.
groups.readingJob: Explain repetition, continuity, intensity, and separate multiplicity of agents, patients, occasions, or places, and show the three prefix formulas as clickable guidance.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the frequentative formation because its lexical availability and shape are not predictable. The application derives the actual copied sounds and all finite consequences from the typed Source.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation with one compact Frequentative Shape choice; do not add controls for copied consonants, vowel length realization, example identity, or meanings that remain contextual readings.

groups.title: Short-glottal ordinary frequentatives
groups.proposal: Use the short-vowel-plus-glottal-stop formation for separately bounded, often intense, abrupt, uneven, or distributive repetition. Offer a compact scope choice only when the intended composition must identify whether actions, participants, occasions, or places are multiplied; otherwise preserve the readings as cues.
groups.writingJob: Build the short-glottal prefix from any compatible open typed Source, preserve participant identity and distributive scope, allow idiomatic or reconstructed Source readings without treating them as productive spelling rules, and support tla fusion and both licensed tla-impersonal placements.
groups.readingJob: Show bounded repetition, intensity, abruptness, unevenness, distributive scope, participant readings, idiomatic meanings, extinct Source analyses, tla fusion, and Canvas examples as non-authorizing evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses short-glottal formation and resolves a scope only when that distinction is needed by the final semantic composition. The application derives the prefix, participant consequences, fusion, and licensed tla placement.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Frequentative Shape and a conditional compact Scope choice; do not add controls for example stems, copied segments, idiomatic glosses, or object forms fixed by the typed Source.

groups.title: Long and short formations, supportive i, and recursion
groups.proposal: Keep long-vowel and short-vowel frequentatives as genuine lexical formation choices. Derive ordinary supportive-i deletion from Source shape, ask for an initial-i history only when supportive and real i are both licensed analyses, and let the user add another reduplication layer when emphatic recursion is intended.
groups.writingJob: Generate long- or short-vowel reduplication from an open typed Source, derive the copied segment after supportive i plus two consonants, preserve exceptional real-i and reconstructed histories, and apply any selected recursive layers through the same reduplication operation.
groups.readingJob: Explain smooth continuous long-vowel repetition, the less common short-vowel formation, supportive-i deletion, exceptional real-i treatment, extinct Sources, compound scope, recursion, and example meanings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses long versus short formation, resolves supportive versus real initial i only when genuinely ambiguous, and chooses additional reduplication layers for intended insistence or emphasis. The application derives every copied segment and boundary change.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Frequentative Shape, conditional Initial-i Analysis, and Add another derivation; do not expose manual copied-sound, deletion, compound-scope, or example controls.

groups.title: Object-pronoun reduplication
groups.proposal: Allow the user to choose the licensed reduplication target when the typed Source contains fused tla or a mainline reflexive before supportive i. Derive tla reduplication, optional further lexical-stem reduplication, and partial reflexive m-o, n-o, or t-o reduplication automatically.
groups.writingJob: Apply object-pronoun reduplication only to a structurally licensed typed Source, preserve independent event and object scopes, allow fused tla and lexical stem to be reduplicated together, delete supportive i where required, and derive the partial reflexive carrier without stem whitelists.
groups.readingJob: Show the selected reduplication target, tla-fusion history, independent object and event scopes, reflexive carrier, supportive-i deletion, participant readings, and example evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses whether licensed reduplication targets fused tla, the lexical stem, both, or the mainline reflexive. The application derives the object form, copied material, supportive-i deletion, and participant structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Show Reduplication Target only for fused-tla or eligible reflexive Sources; do not add manual tla shape, reflexive-prefix, copied-vowel, object-scope, or example controls.

groups.title: Intransitive destockal frequentatives
groups.proposal: Let a typed first-kind destockal Source use either the ordinary frequentative or the special destockal formation when that lexical choice is intended. For the special formation, replace ni or licensed hui with ca, add short-vowel reduplication, derive stock-vowel realization, Class A, recursion, and the licensed impersonal paths automatically.
groups.writingJob: Recognize any open typed first-kind destockal shape, derive ni or hui to ca with short-vowel reduplication, preserve its distinct meaning, support recursive reduplication, form ca-to-c-ō or c-o-hua nonactive stems and impersonal tla formations, and assign Class A without example-stem gates.
groups.readingJob: Explain ordinary versus special frequentatives, reduced stock-vowel quantity, semantic contrasts, recursive intensity, nonactive and impersonal restrictions, tla intensification, Class A behavior, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses ordinary versus special destockal frequentative, intended recursion, and an existing Voice choice. The application derives suffix replacement, vowel realization, class, nonactive shape, and impersonal consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Frequentative Type, Add another derivation, and Voice; do not add controls for ca replacement, stock-vowel marking, Class A, nonactive allomorph, tla placement fixed by the selected path, or examples.

groups.title: Causative destockal frequentatives
groups.proposal: For an open typed first-kind causative destockal Source, let the user select the special frequentative and derive replacement of n, ni, or hua with tz while retaining causative a and adding short-vowel reduplication.
groups.writingJob: Derive the causative destockal frequentative from Source suffix shape, preserve causative force and object structure, realize the reduced stock vowel, assign Class B, and drop final a in the perfective through the normal class machinery.
groups.readingJob: Show the Source suffix, retained causative a, replacement by tz, short-vowel prefix, reduced stock vowel, Class B perfective, participant structure, lexical readings, and example evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the special causative destockal frequentative when intended. The application derives replacement, reduplication, class, perfective, and participants.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Frequentative Type; do not add controls for tz, retained a, copied sounds, stock-vowel marking, Class B, perfective loss, or examples.

groups.title: Extinct, fused, and role-ambiguous destockals
groups.proposal: Accept an extinct or fused destockal history as a typed Source analysis rather than an example-stem exception. Preserve the fused long vowel, and expose Causative versus Applicative only where a frequentative tz-a Result genuinely permits both interpretations.
groups.writingJob: Apply the licensed extinct or fused destockal analysis to any matching open typed Source shape, retain fused vowel length, generate its frequentative Result, preserve both causative and applicative structures when licensed, and let context or composition select the intended role.
groups.readingJob: Show reconstructed Source history, fused-vowel preservation, lexical survival, tz-a structure, causative-applicative ambiguity, contextual selection, participant consequences, and Canvas examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies an unresolved extinct or fused Source history and chooses Causative versus Applicative only when final composition requires one. The application derives form, vowel quantity, and participant structure while preserving unresolved readings.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse conditional Source History and Derivation Role choices; never use the listed stems as a whitelist and do not add controls for fused vowel length or example meaning.

groups.title: Destockal applicative and rare Type-two causative
groups.proposal: Reuse the ordinary derivation choices on a completed frequentative destockal Result: Applicative changes tz-a to ch-i and adds liā, while the rare Type-two causative is selected only when lexically licensed. The user chooses the derivation and any new participant; the application derives the form and hierarchy.
groups.writingJob: Recapture an open typed frequentative destockal Result, derive tz-a to ch-i-liā for Applicative or the licensed Type-two causative, import the new participant, preserve existing objects, reject unsupported tla fusion, and use the shared applicative and causative machinery.
groups.readingJob: Show the recaptured Result, replaced suffix, added applicative, rare Type-two route, object hierarchy, beneficiary or causee, rejected analyses, source criticism, and example evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Applicative or rare Type-two Causative when intended and supplies the new participant. The application derives the suffix sequence, class, object hierarchy, and realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Add another derivation, Derivation Type, and participant identity; do not add controls for ch-i, liā, object levels, class, unsupported historical analyses, or examples.

groups.title: Uncertain ca frequentatives
groups.proposal: Treat the uncertain ca family as an explicit typed analysis, not an example-stem whitelist: add ca to an open root with the selected reduplicative formation, and allow the related tz-a counterpart, applicative participant, or fused-tla lexicalization only when the intended structure calls for it.
groups.writingJob: Build the ca-family analysis from an open typed root and shape, preserve its uncertain history, derive related tz-a structure and participant changes, apply authorized assimilation and tla fusion structurally, and avoid inferring a lexical meaning for an arbitrary Source.
groups.readingJob: Explain uncertain derivation, auditory or visual and onomatopoeic tendencies, ca and tz-a comparison, causative or applicative force, fusion, reconstructed Sources, assimilation, lexical meanings, and Canvas examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the uncertain ca analysis and any real Causative versus Applicative, participant, or fusion interpretation needed for the intended composition. The application derives the matching shape and structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source Analysis, Derivation Role, participant, and fusion choices only when structurally relevant; never present the Canvas examples as the allowable Source inventory.

groups.title: Uncertain tz-ca frequentatives
groups.proposal: Treat the uncertain tz-ca family as a shape-based typed analysis: replace the final Source syllable with tz-ca and add the selected reduplicative prefix. Keep unreduplicated and transitive tz-ca structures distinct, and do not restrict the operation to Canvas example stems.
groups.writingJob: Apply final-syllable replacement and reduplication to an open compatible typed Source, preserve a completed tz-ca Result for later causative derivation, distinguish unreduplicated or transitive tz-ca analyses, and derive sound changes from structure rather than spelling lists.
groups.readingJob: Show the replaced Source syllable, tz-ca, reduplicative prefix, uncertain history, comparison with ca and destockal families, later causative route, unreduplicated and transitive contrasts, relic analysis, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the uncertain tz-ca analysis and resolves a genuinely different unreduplicated or transitive Source analysis when needed. The application performs replacement, reduplication, and later typed derivation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source Analysis and Add another derivation; do not add an example-stem picker or controls for replaced syllables, copied segments, lexical glosses, or relic comparisons.

groups.title: Frequentative nonactive
groups.proposal: Allow frequentative derivation on any canonical nonactive Result. The user chooses the frequentative formation on that recaptured Result; the application preserves impersonal voice and derives the reading of separate individual acts within the collective action.
groups.writingJob: Recapture an owner-issued nonactive Result as the Source for frequentative derivation, preserve its voice and participant topology, derive the selected reduplicative form, and pass the completed Result through ordinary Mood and Tense realization.
groups.readingJob: Show the nonactive Source link, impersonal group, separately distributed individual acts, reduplicative structure, tense or aspect contribution, alternative readings, and example evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the frequentative formation on the nonactive Result and any ordinary Mood or Tense needed for the sentence. The application derives voice continuity, distribution, and surface realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Add another derivation, Frequentative Shape, Mood, and Tense; do not add Lesson-27-specific impersonal, participant-distribution, or example controls.
